features.title: 3D objects as short programs
features.what: Parts, solids, edits and assemblies are written as Python over bpy.
features.evidence_quote: sand3d is a Python library for writing 3D objects as short programs: profiles, solids, edits, frames, joints and assemblies, over Blender's bpy.

features.title: Few tokens per part
features.what: A part costs two to six times fewer tokens than in Blender Python or CadQuery.
features.evidence_quote: Short. A part takes 2 to 6× fewer tokens than the same part in Blender Python, CadQuery or FeatureScript

features.title: Named, not computed
features.what: Parts, edges and faces are addressed by name, never by coordinates.
features.evidence_quote: Named, not computed. Parts, edges and faces are reached by name, never by hand-computed coordinates.

features.title: Deterministic builds
features.what: The same program produces the same mesh, bit for bit.
features.evidence_quote: Deterministic. The same program builds the same mesh, bit for bit.

features.title: Exports real formats
features.what: One call writes GLB, URDF, USD, OBJ or STL named by the file extension.
features.evidence_quote: One call; the file's extension names the format; lengths in metres.

features.title: Whole API in a prompt
features.what: The documented API fits in a prompt at about 3,600 tokens.
features.evidence_quote: The whole API fits in a prompt, about 3,600 tokens

features.title: bpy version limits
features.what: Blender's bpy module only ships for some Python versions and some Macs.
features.evidence_quote: bpy has no wheel for Python 3.12, nor for Intel Macs from 5.2 on: there, use Python 3.11.

risks.text: It depends on Blender's bpy module, so the Python version and the machine both matter.
There are no category verbs: a chair or a table is a program you write in sand3d.
